Hi Sara — really appreciate the thorough list. Answering inline and attaching a concise matrix for your model: SLA_Matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet).

- Uptime bands: we publish four standard tiers (99.5%, 99.9%, 99.95%, 99.99%). For pilots we typically start at 99.9% for hosted and 99.95% for dedicated pools. The attached sheet maps credit percentages per band.
- Minimum commits: to qualify for the 4-hour guaranteed response lane and 24/7 on-call escalation, we require a minimum monthly commit of $30k or a 6-month reserved capacity purchase. We can consider a reduced commit with a one-time premium.
- Custom lanes: yes — we can create a custom lane for your checkout Sev 1 with a 4-hour business-hours response (Mon-Fri 7a-7p PT). That would be billed as an add-on to any tier; I put an example price in the sheet.

Per your ask, I looped in our Pricing & Ops lead (Olga) and Finance (Laura) to confirm the commercial wiggle room. If this looks good I can produce a clean SOW and a draft crediting clause for legal.

Sara / Tessa — adding some technical and operational color so BrightCart can weigh trade-offs.

1) Latency vs. uptime: For checkout-critical workloads we recommend dedicated pools with pinning to selected regions — this reduces noisy-neighbor risk and supports hot-warm failover. Dedicated increases base cost ~25-40% vs hosted at comparable SLOs, but it cuts variance and makes 99.95/99.99 realistic.

2) Response ladder and on-call: Our standard response tiers map to Severity definitions in the sheet. To guarantee a 4-hour business-hours response for a labeled Sev 1 incident we commit a local escalation engineer and a prioritized triage queue. That is normally included only for our 99.95 and 99.99 bands with the $30k+ monthly commit, but Tessa flagged a potential pilot concession.

3) Credits and windows: Credits are calculated as % of monthly invoice and tier up per downtime bucket. We can structure a capped credit ladder (e.g., max 50% credit in any month) to limit financial exposure.

Operational ask: if BrightCart wants a hybrid band (hosted for non-critical routes, dedicated for checkout), we should define routing policies, cache affinity, and footprint so we can size the dedicated pool. I can run a sizing estimate if you share 7-day peak qps and avg seq length.

TL;DR: custom 4-hour business-hours lane is feasible — requires either the commit level or a short pilot premium.

—Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
